The car company Ford is now complaining about a government rule that requires it to sell a certain `figure` of electric cars each year, calling the whole `operation` unworkable. The strange part is that just two years ago, Ford was a huge supporter of this exact rule and even wanted the government to make the sales targets higher for every car `group`.

female customers and male customers alike are buying electric cars more slowly than automakers predicted. Back in 2022, companies thought their investment in electric cars would quickly bear `fruit`. Now, Ford has joined a `group` of other carmakers to `sing` a different tune, complaining that the government's rules are too tough because of this slowdown in sales.

This big change in Ford's opinion happened because the market has shifted. During the pandemic, it was easy to sell cars. But now that the economy is tougher, not as many people are buying electric cars as the companies had planned for. The industry was not prepared for this change in customer demand.

P.P.S This situation shows how quickly business plans can become outdated when the economy changes.
